editorial.headline: Other-Material Furniture, Open Nationally, Blocked in Bali
editorial.standfirst: KBLI 31029 covers furniture made from materials outside the main named furniture categories, but Bali currently blocks PMA registration under its risk moratorium.
editorial.body:
KBLI 31029 is for a particular corner of furniture manufacturing: furniture whose main material is not wood, rattan, bamboo, metal, plastic, or imitation goods. In practical terms, the record places tables, chairs, stools, beds, cupboards, shelving, and room partitions inside the field when they are made from these other materials. It also includes mattress and bedding-related production: mattress or bed complements, spring-filled or stuffed mattresses, mattresses filled with kapok or dacron, and uncoated plastic or rubber mattresses and similar goods.

The category is not limited to the familiar furniture showroom object. The scope also reaches furniture made from plant fibres, and even decorative restaurant carts such as dessert carts and food carts. That makes this a manufacturing code for makers working outside the dominant material families, rather than a general trade or retail description. The substance is production: making the furniture or mattress-type goods described in the record.

On the national investment reading, the code is open. The slim record marks the PMA status as TERBUKA and gives the maximum foreign ownership figure as 100%, with the source stated as Perpres 10/2021, 49/2021. It is also open across Mikro, Kecil, Menengah, and Besar scales. Taken nationally, that is a clean signal: the record does not show a foreign-share cap below full ownership, and it does not narrow the activity to only one business scale.

Bali is the harder part, and it changes the practical answer for a foreign-owned setup on the island. The record marks the Bali side as blocked, with the reason: “OSS risk at scale Besar is Rendah/Menengah-Rendah on every scope → blocked by Bali moratorium 13 May 2026.” The moratorium rule in the record says Bali province blocks all Low and Medium-Low risk KBLI for PMA, island-wide and permanently. So the honest conclusion is that KBLI 31029 may be nationally foreign-open, but a foreigner cannot register this activity as PMA in Bali today under the Bali-side record provided here.
